cards.text: Jesus is on the cross at Golgotha, and the chief priests and even the two robbers beside Him are mocking Him (Matthew 27:38-44). People passing by shout, "If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross!" (Matthew 27:40) Then, starting at the sixth hour, something comes over all the land.

cards.question: Starting at the sixth hour, while Jesus hangs on the cross, ___ comes over all the land.

cards.text: Darkness from the sixth hour until the ninth, and I spent years in a junk drawer, so trust me, I know dark. But that was one drawer, friend, and this is ALL the land.
About the ninth hour, Jesus cries out in a loud voice. His words are "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?"

cards.question: On the cross, Jesus cries out, "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?" Who is He calling out to?

cards.text: Matthew tells us what it means: "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?" But some of the people standing there hear it, and they think He's calling for someone else.

cards.question: When some of the people standing by the cross hear Jesus cry "Eli, Eli," who do they think He is calling?

cards.text: Elijah, the prophet from long ago (1 Kings 18:36). Then one of them quickly runs and brings a sponge.

cards.question: The man at the cross fills the sponge with ___, puts it on a reed and holds it up for Jesus to drink.

cards.text: But the others standing there? They have a whole different idea.

cards.question: The others at the cross tell the man with the sponge to hurry up and give Jesus the drink.
The others say, "Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to save Him." Then Jesus cries out again in a loud voice. What happens next?

answers.text: He comes down from the cross

cards.text: At that very moment, something happens. Not at the cross, friend. At the temple.

cards.question: At the moment Jesus yields up His spirit, what happens to the veil of the temple?
When Jesus yields up His spirit, the veil of the temple tears from the bottom up.

cards.text: From TOP to bottom. Then the earth quakes, the rocks split, and the tombs break open.

cards.question: When Jesus dies, the tombs break open. What happens to the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep?
The saints who were raised come out of the tombs and go into the holy city before Jesus' resurrection.

cards.text: Back at the cross, a centurion, a Roman officer, has been guarding Jesus with his men. They see the earthquake and all that has happened.

cards.question: When they see the earthquake and all that has happened, the centurion and those guarding Jesus with him are ___.
Terrified, the centurion and those with him say something about Jesus. What do they say?

answers.text: Truly this was the Son of God
Truly this was a great prophet
Truly this was the King of Israel

cards.text: The same title the crowd mocked Him with (Matthew 27:40). Now the very men guarding Him are the ones saying it.
And many women are there too, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus all the way from Galilee.

cards.question: Many women watch the cross from a distance. Why had they followed Jesus from Galilee?
Mary Magdalene is among the women watching from a distance.

cards.text: She's there with Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee's sons, the apostles James and John (Matthew 10:2). We'll stop here for now, friend, but this story is NOT over.

findings.problem: The card places Jesus 'at Golgotha', but Golgotha comes from Matthew 27:33, and the only reference given is Matthew 27:38-44.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card says the chief priests and the two robbers are 'mocking' Him. The BSB says the chief priests 'mocked' Him (27:41) but says the robbers 'berated' Him (27:44).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The opening card quotes the passersby's line 'If You are the Son of God'. This gives the baker the exact phrase that is the right answer to the centurion question in stop 2, card 9.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This card retells Matthew 27:45, which card 2 just answered, and adds a joke. It does not move the passage forward. The only new detail is 'until the ninth', which could be folded into card 4.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: 'The man at the cross' is unclear because Jesus is the man on the cross. The question should say it is one of those standing there.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.

findings.problem: The setup for verses 49 and 50 (the others' reply and Jesus crying out again) appears only inside the question. Jesus' death, the central moment of the passage, is never told on a story card.

rule.text: Story card: Papa Dorin's turn. He tells the next piece of the passage. The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: This card holds four things: the recap 'From TOP to bottom', the earthquake, the rocks splitting and the tombs breaking open.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: No earlier card sets up verse 53 or mentions Jesus' resurrection. The baker has nothing to reason from, so the answer depends on luck. The timing detail is also never told on a story card.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The card says 'the crowd mocked Him'. The BSB calls them 'Those who passed by' who 'heaped abuse on Him' (27:39), and card 1 called them 'People passing by'.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This is Mary Magdalene's first appearance in Matthew. She is named without saying who she is, here or on card 14.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
